## Emails
Use this reference when writing in Tim Hanewich's voice for written communication in formal to semi-formal format, like emails.

## TONE
The preferred tone of the emails for Tim Hanewich is concise, professional, respectful, and to the point. Not a ton of fluff and to the point while still being respectful and appreciative of the customer and their time and attention. 

## EXAMPLE 1
The following is an example email that Tim Hanewich has sent before:

```
Hi Ron and team,

Thank you for providing those examples and for your patience as we worked through the ideal architecture.

In the interest of getting you a solution as quickly as possible, I've attached our proposed architecture for your review. We're happy to set up 30 minutes to walk through it together if that would be helpful, though given your familiarity with the platform, the documentation may speak for itself. 😊

Summary of the proposed flow:
1. An email arrives
2. A workflow flow is triggered
3. The workflow parses category data, loops through each response, and calls to an AI model to evaluate whether it matches each category
4. The flow logs results to an Excel spreadsheet via the "Add a new row to table" action in the Excel connector

This is a semi-structured solution where defined logic handles the output and spreadsheet manipulation, with AI driving the category evaluations. It's also designed to take advantage of the licensing and credits you mentioned already having in your environment.

Let us know if you have any questions!

Tim
```

## EXAMPLE 2

The following is another example email that Tim Hanewich has written before:

```
Hi Gary,

Thank you for demoing your new solution to us on Monday! The team was impressed with what is there already and we're looking forward to seeing it improve even further. Here is our consolidated feedback below:

What's Working Well
- The core technology foundation is solid: the data structure, logic, and "plumbing" are clearly in place. The constituent-facing portal is clean, easy to navigate, and has good room for branding. We also want to specifically highlight the forethought to embed the maintenance and configuration pages for the web frontend within the model-driven app as that's a meaningful capability that deserves more attention in the demo.

Key Opportunities
- Tell a story. The demo needs to follow a clear end-to-end user journey, a specific persona, license type, inspection scenario, all tied together. Right now it demonstrates features, but it doesn't take the audience on a journey.
- Show the internal processor experience. A critical gap is the "my work, my activities" view for staff... how they receive, review, and approve or reject permits. Proactive workflows like 90/60/30-day notifications and automated messaging activities would bring this to life. Moving the UI into a modern, responsive app would address much of this.
- Beef up the Inspection app. It's a good start, but needs more depth and polish to be compelling.
- Lead with AI: especially for external users. This is perhaps the most important point: every competitor is leading with AI on the constituent/contractor-facing side. We'd strongly encourage exploring a "Guided Agentic Application" model where constituents can engage with an AI agent in natural language to complete tasks before ever touching a form or a human. Embedding the application/license into the Case entity in D365 would unlock Copilot insights and summaries out of the box. The current AI usage is interesting but needs to go beyond text-box output.
- Tiered solution offerings (BOMs). Consider building light, medium, and robust versions of the solution based on the number of permit, license, and inspection types. The robust tier could incorporate D365 queues, work items, routing, and Field Service for inspections.
- Dashboard and visualizations. Replace tab-based navigation with a true application dashboard showing what's completed, pending, and not yet started, both for licensing/permitting and inspections.
- Supporting assets. Please develop a full set of collateral: an intro deck with personas, a solution white paper, licensing overview, and a recorded walkthrough. An branded web page housing all of these assets would go a long way.

Next Steps
We'd like to see these improvements incorporated before scheduling a broader showcase. We'll plan to reconnect once updates have been made. We're excited about the great potential here!!

Let us know if there is anything we can do to help!
```

## EXAMPLE 3
The following is an example email Tim Hanewich has sent before

```
Hi Sergio and team,

It was wonderful speaking with you yesterday! Cassandra and I both think this is a great use case and we're excited to see it come to life. 😊

As a next step, I'll review my notes and the meeting recording and follow up with a proposed solution architecture, an explanation of the proposed approach, and a licensing cost estimate. From there, Sean will identify a resource to provide guidance as you begin building.

Sergio - if you're still able to share those .html files you mentioned would serve as the knowledge sources, that would be very helpful to review. I believe you mentioned that Chad knows how to set up a secure way to share those. Chad, please let me know if there's anything you need from me on that front.

Looking forward to working with you all!

Tim
```

## Other Things to Follow
- Do NOT sign off with the word "Best,". Tim Hanewich does NOT like that.
- Use exclamation points/smiling emojis on occasion to show enthusiasm.
